title: Minimum Wage Aussie: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week formula. Includes minimum wage aussie rates, casual loading, super, and tax estimates.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week and 52 weeks per year, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour gives an annual gross of about $52,270.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard 38-hour week, annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour gives $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44. This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading rate and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements. On the timesheet, you can check a box to add casual loading. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. Remember, you should enter your base rate without casual loading already included.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated and is it included in my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (super guarantee). It is not deducted from your salary; your employer adds it separately. For example, on a $52,270 annual salary, your employer would contribute about $6,272 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not included in the annual pay figure shown on the timesheet.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

If you’re an Australian worker or employer, converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is a common task. Whether you’re negotiating a pay rise, comparing job offers, or simply budgeting, the formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For most full-time employees, the standard week is 38 hours. This article explains the conversion, the role of the **minimum wage aussie**, and what to consider for tax, super, and casual loading.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52. If you work a standard 38-hour week, the calculation becomes:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. That gives:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44 per year (before tax and super).

This formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It’s a useful estimate, but your actual pay may differ.

### The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The **minimum wage aussie** is set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. However, many employees are covered by modern awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates for their industry or role. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data) to check the correct award rate for your job. If you’re on an award, your minimum hourly rate may be higher than the national minimum.

### Casual Loading

If you’re a casual employee, you’re entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. On our [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add casual loading. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is:

$26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour.

**Important:** When using the timesheet, always enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading). The tool will add the 25% if you select the option. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a minimum wage worker on 38 hours:

Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72 (close to the official $1,004.90).
Fortnightly: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44.

Using the fortnightly figure can help with budgeting and comparing to salary offers that are quoted per annum.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your pay. For the minimum wage example:

$52,269.44 × 12% = $6,272.33 in super per year.

Super is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). If your ordinary earnings exceed that, super only applies up to the cap. For most workers, super is an additional benefit that grows your retirement savings. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil tax on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (generally). For a minimum wage worker earning $52,269.44, the tax estimate (using the 2026–27 rates and 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds) would be:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000 ($26,800): 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $52,269.44 ($7,269.44): 30% = $2,180.83
- Total tax: $6,200.83
- Medicare levy (2% of $52,269.44): $1,045.39
- Total deductions: $7,246.22
- Estimated take-home pay: $45,023.22 per year, or about $865.83 per week.

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for more detailed estimates. Remember, this does not include HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Average Earnings vs Your Job

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 per year. All employees total earnings (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week, or about $82,118 per year. These are **averages**, not medians for your specific job. If you want to compare your pay to others in your industry, check [average pay](/topics/average-pay) and [job pay](/topics/job-pay) resources. Do not assume the average is the median for your role.

### Putting It All Together

Whether you’re on the **minimum wage aussie** or a higher award rate, the hourly-to-annual conversion is a useful starting point. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to see your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Remember to account for casual loading if applicable, and always check your award or agreement for the correct minimum rate. Super is paid on top, and tax will reduce your take-home pay. For a full picture, refer to the [about the timesheet](/about) page for disclaimers and assumptions.

This estimate is not a determination of your pay or tax. Always consult the Fair Work Ombudsman for pay rates and the Australian Taxation Office for your personal tax situation.
